title: Denmark 2-3 Norway: Haaland completes comeback to book quarter-final spot
subtitle: Norway needed a win to reach the last eight of the Nations League, and they got it in the dying seconds to leapfrog Denmark in the table.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland's 96th-minute penalty earned Norway a dramatic 3-2 win over Denmark to pip Brian Riemer's side to the Nations League quarter-finals.
Norway knew only a win would be enough to get them into the knockout stage, but they started poorly as Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a 2-0 lead inside 14 minutes.
However, Haaland halved the deficit before the break, and scored the winning penalty – after Martin Odegaard had equalised – to help Norway finish second in Group A4.
Torbjorn Heggem got to Joakim Maehle's throughball into the box, but his backpass beat Orjan Nyland, allowing Hojlund to convert on the line 11 minutes in.
Isaksen then teed up their second with a looping right-sided cross, and Hojbjerg was unmarked as he peeled away at the far post, nodding in from a tight angle.

Haaland had one goal disallowed just after the half-hour mark as he nodded the ball against his arm on its way into the net, but his 37th-minute effort stood. Odegaard caught Mads Hermansen on the ball with his heavy touch turned in by the striker.
Sander Berge saw a header cleared off the line before the break, while Haaland's next big chance saw him uncharacteristically blaze over from just inside the box.
Kristoffer Ajer then hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, but Norway's pressure eventually told, as Odegaard fired in the rebound after Andreas Schjelderup hit the post in the 83rd minute.

Haaland had the final say, with Joachim Andersen penalised for a handball in the box as he attempted to clear, and the Manchester City man coolly slotted into the bottom-right corner to complete the turnaround.

Things had been looking pretty bleak for Norway at the start of the international break, but they kept fighting to the final minute to finish above Denmark – on their head-to-head record – to avoid the League A/B play-offs.

Haaland's goalscoring record is formidable, and he has now netted 68 goals in 61 appearances for Norway, with his tally in the Nations League now sitting at 25 goals, more than any other player since the tournament's inception in 2018.
He only had 23 touches throughout, but he led Norway for shots (seven), attempts on target (three), touches in the opposition box (10) and Opta-defined 'big' chances (four).
Haaland also accumulated 2.43 expected goals (xG) of Norway's 3.89 total, and he finished with more than Denmark (1.61 xG) managed from their seven total shots.
It had all started so well for Denmark, who simply needed to avoid defeat to reach the quarter-finals, but instead they enter the play-offs after failing to build on their strong start at Parken.

Norway knew only a win would be enough to get them into the knockout stage, but they started poorly as Rasmus Hojlund and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg gave Denmark a 2-0 lead inside 14 minutes.

However, Haaland halved the deficit before the break, and scored the winning penalty – after Martin Odegaard had equalised – to help Norway finish second in Group A4.

Torbjorn Heggem got to Joakim Maehle's throughball into the box, but his backpass beat Orjan Nyland, allowing Hojlund to convert on the line 11 minutes in.

Isaksen then teed up their second with a looping right-sided cross, and Hojbjerg was unmarked as he peeled away at the far post, nodding in from a tight angle.

Sander Berge saw a header cleared off the line before the break, while Haaland's next big chance saw him uncharacteristically blaze over from just inside the box.

Kristoffer Ajer then hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, but Norway's pressure eventually told, as Odegaard fired in the rebound after Andreas Schjelderup hit the post in the 83rd minute.

Haaland had the final say, with Joachim Andersen penalised for a handball in the box as he attempted to clear, and the Manchester City man coolly slotted into the bottom-right corner to complete the turnaround.

Who else but Haaland?

Things had been looking pretty bleak for Norway at the start of the international break, but they kept fighting to the final minute to finish above Denmark – on their head-to-head record – to avoid the League A/B play-offs.

Haaland's goalscoring record is formidable, and he has now netted 68 goals in 61 appearances for Norway, with his tally in the Nations League now sitting at 25 goals, more than any other player since the tournament's inception in 2018.

Haaland also accumulated 2.43 expected goals (xG) of Norway's 3.89 total, and he finished with more than Denmark (1.61 xG) managed from their seven total shots.

It had all started so well for Denmark, who simply needed to avoid defeat to reach the quarter-finals, but instead they enter the play-offs after failing to build on their strong start at Parken.
